historical_references.reference: The name 'Kumara' is associated with several deities in Hindu mythology. One of the most famous is Kartikeya, also known as Skanda or Murugan. He is considered the god of war and son of Shiva and Parvati. The story goes that Parvati created Kartikeya to lead an army against a demon named Taraka who was tormenting the gods. After Kartikeya's victory, he was given the title 'Kumara' which means 'prince' or 'youth'.

Another reference to the name 'Kumara' comes from the epic Mahabharata. In this context, 'Kumara' is the name of a king of the Lunar Dynasty, who ruled over the ancient city of Hastinapura. He is described as a great warrior and the son of Bhishma. Kumara is also known as Dhrishtadyumna, and he played a significant role in the great battle of Kurukshetra between the Pandavas and the Kauravas.
